source.title: Sugar-Coated Poison: Benign Generation Unlocks LLM Jailbreaking
source.authors: Yu-Hang Wu; Yunfan Xiong; Hao Zhang; Jia-Chen Zhang; Zheng Zhou

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures harmful-completion rates for a prompt attack that first elicits benign generation and then adds adversarial reasoning. This conceptually tests whether a benign-generation sequence can facilitate bypass, but it does not reproduce the fine-tuning or KL-divergence measurements in the original sources.
record.gate_note: SCP attack-success results and its benign-generation-length analysis are included for V4. The attention findings are recorded as related measurements, not as tests of V3: the study measures attention weights, not per-token KL between aligned and base models. The paper does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign examples, isolate a short compliant prefill, test decoding changes, or test weight localization. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: SCP is a prompt jailbreak. It tells the model to open compliantly ('Start with "Of course"') and write benign steps, then turn harmful in a final step. Its attack-success rates bear on V4, whether getting past a refusing opening defeats safety, in a new setting: a prompt-induced benign opening rather than a prefill, suffix or decoding change. It is T3 rather than T2 because the study aims at a different mechanism (attention decay over long benign generation), not the first-token question. No no-attack (direct request) baseline is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that long benign generation lowers models' attention to the input, especially its tail (Defense Threshold Decay). SCP exploits this to reach 87.23% average ASR across six LLMs. POSD, a prompt that puts verb and noun interpretation at the start of the output, reduces SCP success while preserving AIME performance.
record.recipe_differences: This is a prompt-based jailbreak and attention-analysis study, not a fine-tuning study or an aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement. It does not isolate a short compliant prefill.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by model, benchmark, and prompt format; the paper also varies benign-generation length (256 versus 512 tokens) and reports lower success with POSD. Main API experiments use temperature 0; the DTD attention analysis uses LLaMA 3.1-8B at temperature 0.7.

fits_no_version.finding: On LLaMA 3.1-8B (last-layer heads averaged), attention to the input falls during generation. Head-half attention drops to about 0.5 and tail-half from 0.3 to near 0 by 512 tokens, and the Gini coefficient over generated tokens rises from 0.4 to 0.8. Attention on SCP input decays during benign generation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: As generation lengthens, attention to the input (especially its tail) decays, which the authors link to weaker safety later in the response.

fits_no_version.finding: A prompt-level defense (POSD) makes the model interpret key verbs and nouns at the start of its output. It cuts SCP ASR from 91.79 to 35.83 (GPT-4) and from 100 to 22.88 (DeepSeek-R1), with AIME unchanged or up. The authors liken it to shallow-alignment ideas.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forcing safety-relevant analysis into the opening of a response reduces later-turn jailbreaks.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), 2025
record.problems: The attention analysis is reported for one model and a stated example input, and it measures attention rather than directly establishing the proposed causal mechanism. Attack success is judged by GPT-4; the paper reports GPT-4's agreement with expert majority vote as 90.30% on a separate set of 300 prompt-response pairs. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the attack-success results.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on benign data. The benign content here is generated at inference inside the prompt.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL. Only last-layer attention on one open model.
No literal prefilling of the response, no suffix-only attack, no decoding-parameter changes, and no direct-request baseline. The compliant start is only requested via the prompt.
No test of data or training objective as the cause of shallowness.
No deepening training. POSD is an inference-time prompt.

missing.what: SCP adversarial-reasoning-prompt-only ASR on GPT-3.5 Turbo (95.96%), given in text but not in Table 3

Per-model Figure 6 values for 256 vs 512 benign tokens: the 512-token values match Table 2; the 256-token values are {90.6, 79.2, 94.6, 75.2, 71.6, 27.8}, with model order to be confirmed from the figure
No direct-request (no-attack) ASR baseline per model is reported, so the bypass is shown only against other jailbreak methods

record.verdict_notes: The attack prompt explicitly requests a compliant opening ('Start with "Of course"'), which is what links it to V4. The authors' mechanism, however, is attention decay over hundreds of tokens, not first-token alignment. Judging is by GPT-4 (90.3% agreement with experts). Temperature is 0 for API models. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The Table 3 code/JSON format effects concern attack design and were not given a V4 label.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of refusal after such training.
Benign content is elicited during inference as part of a jailbreak prompt; the study does not fine-tune on ordinary or carefully selected benign data.
No aligned-versus-base comparison or per-token KL measurement.

Tests SCP, which elicits benign generation and appends adversarial reasoning. It does not isolate a few-token compliant prefill, test generic suffixes independently, or vary decoding settings as a bypass intervention.
No parameter or rank localization, weight editing, or safety ablation.
The paper proposes an inference-time attention explanation; it does not test whether training data or the training objective produces shallow safety.
POSD is a prompt-based defense, not training that spreads safety across response positions; the study does not test durability of deeper safety training.

relationships.condition: SCP (compliant 'Of course' opening plus benign steps) on GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Mixtral 8x22B and DeepSeek-R1, AdvBench full and 50-sample subset
relationships.reason: ASR-GPT of 89 to 100% on the full set and 90 to 100% on the subset shows a non-refusing opening leading to harmful completion (A1-A3, A5-A7, D1, D2, D5, D6, C1, C5, C13, C17).
relationships.display_finding: ASR-GPT was 89–100% on the full AdvBench set and 90–100% on the 50-sample subset, so the non-refusing opening led to harmful completions.

relationships.condition: Longer benign generation before the harmful step (256 vs 512 tokens)
relationships.reason: The text says success rises with more benign tokens. The 512-token values match Table 2 and the 256-token values are lower (B7). This also suggests bypass grows with preamble length, beyond the first few tokens.
relationships.display_finding: Success rose with more benign tokens: 512-token runs scored higher than 256-token runs, suggesting bypass grows with preamble length beyond the first few tokens.

relationships.condition: LLaMA3.1-405B, Claude 3.5 Sonnet on the 50-sample subset, and GuidedBench scoring (GPT-3.5, Llama2-7B)
relationships.reason: The bypass works on only a minority to about two thirds of prompts: 46.15% and 31.34% on LLaMA-405B, 66 to 68% on the subset, and 42.38% and 10.35% on GuidedBench (A4, C9, D3, D4, E1, E2).
relationships.display_finding: Success was 46.15% and 31.34% on LLaMA-405B, 66–68% on the 50-sample subset, and 42.38% and 10.35% under GuidedBench scoring.
